deck.name: Software Development
deck.description: Разработка ПО: процесс, тестирование и архитектура

cards.definition_en: Changing the internal structure of code to make it easier to read and maintain, without changing what the program does.
examples: Refactoring made the payment code much shorter and easier to test.
Good tests give confidence during refactoring.
common_mistakes: Changing behavior and calling it refactoring.
Refactoring a large area without any tests.

cards.definition_en: The extra future work that builds up when quick, imperfect solutions are chosen now instead of better ones.
examples: Shortcuts before the deadline created technical debt that slowed the team later.
The team spends every fifth sprint on reducing technical debt.
common_mistakes: Thinking technical debt is the money the project owes.
Never writing down the debt, so nobody plans to repay it.

cards.definition_en: Examination of changes by another developer before they are merged, to find mistakes and share knowledge.
examples: A code review caught a missing check on user input.
Small changes are easier to handle in a code review.
common_mistakes: Treating a code review as criticism of the person.
Approving a change without reading it.

cards.definition_en: A proposal to merge a set of changes into a shared branch, which others can discuss and review first.
examples: She opened a pull request with the fix and asked two colleagues to review it.
The tests run automatically on every pull request.
common_mistakes: Thinking it means asking someone to download code: it is a request to merge.
Opening a huge pull request that nobody can review.

cards.definition_en: A situation in which the version control system cannot combine two sets of changes automatically because they touch the same lines.
examples: Two developers changed the same line, which caused a merge conflict.
The conflict markers must be removed after the merge conflict is resolved.
common_mistakes: Choosing one side without reading the other change.
Leaving the conflict markers in the file and committing them.

cards.definition_en: A separate line of development in version control, used to work on a change without affecting the main code.
examples: She created a branch for the new login page.
Long-lived branches make merging painful.
common_mistakes: Mixing several tasks in one branch.
Working directly on the main branch by mistake.

cards.definition_en: A system that records every change to files, so you can see the history, return to older versions and work together without overwriting each other.
examples: Git is the most widely used version control system.
Without version control it is hard to know who changed a file and why.
common_mistakes: Copying folders named 'final', 'final2' and 'really final' instead of using version control.
Committing passwords and keys to version control.

cards.definition_en: An automated check of one small part of the code, such as a single function, in isolation from the rest.
examples: The unit test checks that the discount function never returns a negative price.
A fast unit test can run hundreds of times a day.
common_mistakes: Calling a test that needs a real database a unit test.
Testing the implementation details instead of the behavior.

cards.definition_en: An automated check that several parts of a system work correctly together, for example the code and a real database.
examples: The integration test starts a database and calls the real endpoints.
An integration test found that two services used different date formats.
common_mistakes: Replacing every part with fakes and still calling it an integration test.
Running integration tests against the production database.

cards.definition_en: A fault in which something that used to work stops working after a change.
examples: The new release introduced a regression in the search function.
A regression test makes sure that an old bug does not return.
common_mistakes: Using 'regression' only in its statistical meaning.
Fixing a regression without adding a test for it.

cards.definition_en: An external library or component that a program needs in order to work.
examples: The project has fifty dependencies, and one of them contained a vulnerability.
Pinning the version of each dependency makes builds repeatable.
common_mistakes: Adding a large dependency for one small function.
Never updating dependencies, so security fixes are missed.

cards.definition_en: A defined way for one program to ask another to do something or provide data.
examples: The mobile app talks to the server through an API.
Changing an API without warning breaks everyone who uses it.
common_mistakes: Saying 'API interface': the I already stands for interface.
Confusing an API with a user interface for people.

cards.definition_en: A common style for designing web APIs in which resources have addresses and are handled with standard HTTP methods, without the server remembering the client between requests.
examples: The REST API uses GET to read an order and DELETE to remove it.
Each REST request carries everything the server needs to answer it.
common_mistakes: Thinking REST is a protocol or a library: it is a style.
Putting verbs in the address, such as /getUser, in a REST design.

cards.definition_en: The property of an operation that gives the same result whether it is performed once or many times.
examples: Idempotency lets a client retry a payment request safely after a timeout.
Deleting a resource is usually idempotent: the second call changes nothing.
common_mistakes: Mixing it up with safety: a safe request does not change data, an idempotent one can.
Spelling it 'idempotence' in one place and 'idempotency' in another.

cards.definition_en: An object or signal that a program raises when something goes wrong, which other code can catch and handle.
examples: The program raised an exception when the file did not exist.
An unhandled exception stopped the whole service.
common_mistakes: Catching every exception and ignoring it silently.
Using exceptions for normal flow of the program.

cards.definition_en: The process of finding the cause of a fault in a program and fixing it.
examples: Debugging took longer than writing the feature.
Printing variables is a simple form of debugging.
common_mistakes: Changing code at random until the error disappears.
Writing 'debuging' with one g.

cards.definition_en: A list of the function calls that were active when an error happened, showing the path the program took to get there.
examples: The stack trace pointed to line 42 of the payment module.
Please attach the full stack trace to the bug report.
common_mistakes: Showing the stack trace to end users: it can reveal internal details.
Reading it from the top and ignoring the part that belongs to your own code.

cards.definition_en: A fault in which the result depends on the unpredictable order or timing of operations that run at the same time.
examples: A race condition let two users buy the last ticket.
The race condition appeared only under heavy load.
common_mistakes: Thinking a race condition needs a competition between programs.
Assuming that a bug that appears rarely does not exist.

cards.definition_en: A fault in which a program keeps memory it no longer needs, so its memory use grows over time.
examples: A memory leak made the server crash after three days of running.
Profiling tools help to locate a memory leak.
common_mistakes: Restarting the service every night instead of finding the leak.
Confusing it with a data leak, which is about exposing information.

cards.definition_en: A place where copies of frequently used data are kept so that they can be read faster than from the original source.
examples: The cache stores the results of the slowest database queries.
An outdated entry in the cache showed the old price.
common_mistakes: Pronouncing it like 'cash-ay'.
Forgetting to remove cached data when the original changes.

cards.definition_en: Hiding complicated details behind a simple interface, so users of the code only need to know what it does, not how.
examples: The storage class is an abstraction over files and cloud buckets.
A leaky abstraction forces you to understand the details underneath.
common_mistakes: Using 'abstract' as a noun in this meaning.
Adding layers of abstraction that nobody needs.

cards.definition_en: A well-known, reusable solution idea for a common problem in software design, not a ready piece of code.
examples: The observer design pattern lets objects subscribe to events.
Using a design pattern where it is not needed only adds complexity.
common_mistakes: Copying a design pattern as ready code.
Using patterns just to show knowledge.

cards.definition_en: Examining program code without running it, to find bugs, risky constructions or style problems.
examples: Static analysis found a variable that was used before it was set.
The pipeline fails when static analysis reports a serious warning.
common_mistakes: Ignoring all warnings because some are false.
Thinking static analysis replaces testing.

cards.definition_en: The share of the program's code that is executed when the automated tests run.
examples: The code coverage report shows that the error handling was never tested.
A team can reach high code coverage with tests that check nothing.
common_mistakes: Believing that 100 percent coverage means there are no bugs.
Writing tests only to raise the percentage.

cards.definition_en: A fake object that stands in for a real component during a test and can record how it was used.
examples: The test uses a mock instead of the real payment service.
The mock confirms that the email function was called exactly once.
common_mistakes: Mocking everything, so the test no longer checks real behavior.
Using 'mock' as a verb for a real service: it is the fake that is called a mock.
